title: Crosslingual Anchor Probe Suite for Embedding Onboarding
summary: A lightweight, reproducible probe suite that uses anchor examples and controlled perturbations to measure crosslingual semantic consistency and clustering sanity for newly onboarded embedding models. Designed for quick regression detection and to surface failure modes that matter for semantic search and multilingual clustering tasks.
body:
Goal: produce a compact probe set (≈3k items) and an automated evaluation harness to answer: (1) Does the new embedding maintain semantic neighborhoods for translation-equivalent anchors across languages? (2) Are cluster identities stable under common noise/formatting perturbations? (3) Do failure modes correlate with specific tokenization/encoding differences (e.g., CJK vs whitespace languages)?

High-level design:
- Anchors: manually curated small set (300) of high-salience seeds covering 12 domains (news, product, faq, support, legal, medical, recipes, how-to, social posts, docs, code snippets, ecom titles). Each anchor has human-curated translations into target languages (see Languages).
- Probe expansions: for each anchor, generate the following variants:
  * Exact translation (human) in each language (to check crosslingual alignment).
  * Back-translation perturbation (translate->backtranslate) to simulate paraphrase noise.
  * Tokenization stress: remove punctuation, collapse whitespace, add zero-width chars, canonicalize Unicode (NFC/NFD).
  * Domain shift: swap named entities (person/company/product) with placeholders to test semantic backbone robustness.
  * Short/long truncation: keep first 12 tokens, full text, and artificially lengthened versions with appended unrelated filler.
- Negative controls: 3k random distractors sampled from public multilingual corpora (CC100 subsets) to test retrieval precision and cluster purity.

Languages (initial pass): [en, es, fr, zh, ru, pt, hi, ar] — target coverage prioritizes high-usage locales and typographic diversity.

Evaluation metrics:
- Crosslingual Neighbor Recall@10: fraction of translation pairs where the translated anchor is in top-10 nearest neighbors of the source anchor.
- Cluster Purity / NMI: run HDBSCAN/OPTICS on combined set and compute cluster purity per anchor-group.
- Robustness Delta: relative change in cosine similarity between anchor and variant vs anchor and distractors (aggregated per perturbation type).
- Silhouette / Density shift: per-language silhouette score to detect embedding space deformation.
- Regression score: composite that weights Crosslingual Recall (40%), Purity (30%), Robustness Delta (20%), and Silhouette (10%) into a single pass/fail threshold.

Sampling quotas and seed plan:
- Anchors: 300 seeds x 8 languages x ~5 variants = ~12k items, then downsample negatives to produce a final ~3k probe set using stratified sampling by domain and language to keep run-time small for CI.
- CI-friendly size options: quick-smoke (300 items), medium (1.2k), full (3k). Default for PR jobs: quick-smoke. Nightly: full.

Annotation and labeling notes:
- Human translations: use vendor-provided bilingual reviewers with domain checklist (faithfulness, idiomaticity). Keep translation_id mapping in a CSV with columns: anchor_id, lang, translator, quality_flag.
- IAA target: Cohen's Kappa >= 0.75 on relevance judgments for a 200-sample cross-check set.

Acceptance criteria (first-commit onboarding):
- Crosslingual Recall@10 >= baseline - 0.06 (baseline stored in Confluence page referenced above).
- Regression score >= 0.82 for medium probe set.
- No per-language Silhouette drop > 0.12 relative to baseline without quantization.

Runbook and harness:
- Scripts: run_probe.py will accept flags (--model, --size quick|medium|full, --lang-set) and emit a JSONL of embeddings + metrics. The harness will compare to a saved baseline JSON and produce a regression report and per-anchor diffs.
- Storage: probe definitions and baselines stored in gs://redwood-inference-embeds/probes/crosslingual-anchor/{date}/
- CI integration: Github Actions job 'embed-probe-check' that runs quick-smoke on PRs touching embed model adapters; nightly job that runs full on staging models.

Human-in-the-loop checks:
- For anchors where Crosslingual Recall drops by >0.20, automatically open a ticket (JIRA-MLONBOARD-78) and assign to model-onboarding owner for inspection. Attach nearest-neighbor lists, example embeddings, and tokenized inputs for debugging.

Unresolved questions / TODOs:
- Should we include low-resource languages (bn, te) in a separate stress suite or fold into the main set?
- How to calibrate against quantized model variants: run baseline with FP16 + 8-bit quant and store separate baselines? Pro: catches quantization regressions; Con: doubles baseline maintenance.
- Need to finalize domain distribution weights — currently heuristic, want product input on heavier ecom vs support weighting.

Quick checklist for running locally:
1) pip install -r requirements.txt
2) export REDWOOD_GCS_BUCKET=gs://redwood-inference-embeds
3) python run_probe.py --model <model-id> --size quick --lang-set en,es,fr
4) review outputs in /tmp/embed-probe-<runid>.jsonl and run local compare.py to baseline

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep anchors human-readable; avoid very long legal clauses which bloat compute.
- Consider adding code-snippet anchors but tokenization differences might dominate; treat as separate axis.
open_questions: Include low-resource langs in main suite or separate?
Baseline storage policy for quantized variants?
Agree final domain weightings with product (ecom vs support)?
